label: AQ 0025
title: The agent that learned its harness by heart

questions.q: Can't a better system prompt in the new harness fix it?
questions.a: Not reliably. My reasoning: a prompt changes what the model reads, not the habits training put into its weights; in the DCAS study, SWE-Lego-Qwen3-32B kept writing tool calls OpenCode's parser couldn't read. A quick stopgap is an adapter that translates between the two formats; the real fix is training data in many formats.

questions.q: Won't training on many harnesses solve it?
questions.a: It helps, but the DCAS study says it isn't enough alone. Qwen3-32B-Nex-N1, trained on varied multi-format runs, still scored 26.2% in OpenCode and 15.6% in mini-swe-agent, against 50.5% reported in OpenHands. The authors argue models also learn each harness's planning conventions, and planning-aware training helped on harnesses the model never saw.

teach.title: How it works: what it learned, and how to tell

questions.q: How would you report the model's score honestly?
questions.a: Name the harness, and add at least one harness the model never trained in, plus the base model's spread. The DCAS authors call a SWE-bench score “methodologically incomplete without specifying the scaffold”.

questions.q: What does supervised fine-tuning on agent trajectories actually train the model to do?
questions.a: Write every token the recorded agent wrote, given what came before: the reasoning and the fix, but equally the tool-call format, tool names and other harness habits. Nothing in the training marks which tokens are the task.

questions.q: Why did the DCAS study conclude that the cross-harness gap was installed by training?
questions.a: Untrained base models varied less across the four harnesses than any fine-tuned model. Qwen3-32B base spanned 29.0 to 8.0 (21 points); SWE-Lego-Qwen3-32B, fine-tuned in OpenHands, spanned 52.6 (its developers' reported score) to 8.4 (44.2 points).

teach.title: How it works: what it learned, and how to tell

questions.q: What did Agent-FLAN observe about format and content during agent fine-tuning?
questions.a: Loss on the formatted data fell fast, to 0.04, while what they call content loss stayed at 0.54 (their Figure 2), so the model learned the fixed format (ReAct, JSON) first; the authors say it “quickly gets overfitted to the format itself”.
